During the conference call today discussing Apple's third-quarter 2026 results, CEO Tim Cook took a moment to mark his final earnings call as the company's helmsman and confirmed that incoming CEO John Ternus will preside over future calls. Below is what he said.

Tim Cook attends his final Apple CEO earnings call

Apple is currently holding its quarterly earnings call to discuss the $109.42 billion in revenue it recorded in its third fiscal quarter of 2026.

Before opening the floor to analyst questions, Cook took a moment to reflect on his final earnings call as Apple CEO.

He also confirmed that John Ternus will host the company's quarterly calls going forward — a point that had previously been unclear, since the CEO is not required to participate in these calls.

Below is what he said:

Before we get to questions, I'd like to take a moment to thank all of our shareholders, especially the long-term shareholders who have trusted us over the years, as well as the analysts who have followed our company so closely. As you know, this will be my last earnings call, and John will be hosting these calls going forward. The transition is going smoothly, and I could not be more excited for John in his new role, leading Apple into its next chapter. He is truly a one-of-a-kind leader, and there is no one more fitting to take the helm. As I've said, I've never been more confident in his leadership, in our management team, and in all of the incredible talent across Apple who are committed to making a difference in the lives of our users around the world. The future is bright, and I have never been more optimistic. Thank you, and Kevin and I would now be happy to take your questions.
